subject: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, routing, structured output & 5xx repro

Subject: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, routing, structured output & 5xx repro

Hi Brian / Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can scope implementation and SOW estimates: 

1) Goals from your side:
- Embed semantic search and a reranker into the product search flow (low latency, <= 120ms p95 target)
- Support structured tool-calling for price lookups and inventory checks
- Private data routing for PII-sensitive calls (VPC + optional on-prem connectors)

2) Action items for Storify (please share by EOD Thursday):
- A short architecture diagram showing where you plan to call the Redwood API (edge vs server-proxy) and auth flow
- Sample payloads (max tokens per request, examples of the reranker input/output)
- Logs for the 5xx errors you saw during the POC (timestamps + request ids) — we can use these to repro locally

3) Redwood next steps:
- Dev will share an SDK snippet for server-proxy auth + recommended routing (server-side for private calls)
- We’ll validate the reranker flow and provide a quantization/retry guidance doc
- Schedule a 1-hour debug session to repro the 5xx and tune timeouts if needed

Attachments: redwood-integration-guide.pdf (SDK samples + auth patterns), arch-diagram.png (example routing), error-log-5xx.txt (placeholder for logs — please attach yours)

If you can send the diagram and logs, I’ll loop Dev in and we’ll aim for a debug session Thu/Fri PST.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, routing, structured output & 5xx repro

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear next steps. Attaching the architecture diagram and the logs we collected this morning. High level notes:

- We call Redwood from an internal server-proxy (Node) that attaches our service token (KMS-managed). We prefer server-side routing for inventory/price tool calls so that keys never land in the browser.
- The 5xx spike happened yesterday between 10:12–10:25am PST. We saw 502s and occasional 504s when a batch of embedding requests hit the endpoint; request ids included: req_7b9a, req_7b9b, req_7c01. I’ve included the raw error-log-5xx.txt.
- Sample payload: we send up to 4 candidate passages + user query for rerank (we’re using 512 tokens max), and embeddings calls are batched at size 32 for throughput.

We’d like to rule out: network timeouts from our side, payload shaping for embeddings, and whether continuous batching on Redwood could cause a fallback.

Happy to join a debug session Thu 11:00am PST.

—Brian
Head of Platform Eng, Storify
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Brian Chen <bchen@storify.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, routing, structured output & 5xx repro

Hi Brian — thanks for the logs and diagram, that’s very helpful. A few quick checks and a repro plan before the debug call: 

1) SDK/auth pattern we recommend (server-proxy):
- Use our Node SDK on the backend and store the API key in your KMS. Do not ship keys to the browser. Example snippet (Node):

const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });

// Server route example
app.post('/api/rerank', async (req, res) => {
  const { query, candidates } = req.body;
  const response = await client.rerank({ model: 'rerank-1', input: { query, candidates } , timeoutMs: 10000 });
  res.json(response);
});

2) Timeouts & retry guidance:
- Start with timeoutMs: 10000 for rerank, 20000 for batch embedding calls of size 32.
- Implement exponential backoff with max 3 retries for 502/504.
- If you’re routing through a load balancer, ensure keepalive is enabled and idle timeouts > 60s.

3) Routing & structured tool calling:
- For price/inventory tool-calls, recommend server-proxy + route policy that pins those requests to your private Dedicated pool (if you’re worried about isolation).
- For structured outputs/tool calling, use our function-calling schema; ensure your tool endpoints return a stable JSON schema — we validate on the server side and will return a structured result.

4) Repro plan for 5xx:
- Can you run a short load test that simulates embedding batch size 32 for 2–3 minutes against our staging endpoint and forward logs (include x-request-id header)?
- We’ll run the same test from our infra and compare traces. I opened SUP-8912 to track (linked).

I’ll bring a staging token to the debug call so we can reproduce together. If you can confirm the environment details (Node version, LB, proxy config) ahead of time that will speed things up.

Thanks — Dev
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Brian Chen <bchen@storify.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 07:44:01 -08:00
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, routing, structured output & 5xx repro

Hi Dev — thanks, that snippet is super helpful. Quick answers:
- Node: 18.x, running behind an Nginx reverse proxy with default keepalive 75s.
- We do use an internal LB with a 30s idle timeout (we can bump).
- Will run the staged load test for embedding batch=32 for 2 minutes and send traces + x-request-id.

Also one thing we observed: when embeddings were batched, the client-side payload occasionally included a null passage (we sanitize most inputs but had a recent regression). Could a null item in the batch lead to a 5xx on Redwood?

—Brian
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Brian Chen <bchen@storify.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:15:30 -08:00
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, routing, structured output & 5xx repro

Thanks Brian — good catch about the null passage. In our experience a malformed batch (nulls or non-string items) can cause the model server to return a 400 or, if the batch splitter mishandles it, surface as a 5xx when the downstream encoder fails. Two immediate mitigations:

1) Add a quick input sanitizer before batching to drop/replace nulls and enforce type string. Example (pseudo):
const sanitized = passages.filter(p => typeof p === 'string' && p.length > 0);

2) Temporary workaround: set an allowlist fallback in your rerank route — if sanitized batch size < 2, fall back to single-shot rerank (smaller payloads).

For the debug call, Dev + I will run a focused test on staging to try malformed payloads and surface logs. I’ve updated SUP-8912 with the steps and will attach results.

Also Rishi — I’ll need a quick approval to provide Storify a staging token and a temporary increased rate limit for the debug run.

—Neha
